newsitem.title: USA: Fran gains strength, moves west-northwest.
newsitem.headline: Fran gains strength, moves west-northwest.

text.p: A hurricane warning was in effect for the northwest Bahamas Tuesday as Hurricane Fran moved west-northwest, becoming stronger as it headed toward Florida, the National Hurricane Center said.

At 2:00 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT), Fran's center was near latitude 25.2 north, longitude 72.3 west, or about 320 miles (520 km) east of Nassau in the Bahamas. The storm was moving west-northwest near 13 mph (20 kmh) and forecasters continued to predict a gradual turn toward the northwest Tuesday night or Wednesday morning.
Maximum sustained winds had increased to near 90 mph (150 kmh) and further strengthening was expected.
Hurricane force winds extended outward up to 85 miles (140 km) from the center and tropical storm force winds extended outward up to 175 miles (280 km).
In addition to the hurricane warning for the northwest Bahamas, a tropical storm warning and a hurricane watch are in effect for the central Bahamas from Acklins Island to Cat Island.
A storm warning means storm conditions are expected within 24 hours, while a watch means such conditions are due within 36 hours.
